newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh tribal rebels deny attacks on army post.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh tribal rebels deny attacks on army post.

text.p: Tribal rebels in Bangladesh's southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts on Saturday denied involvement in a recent shootout at an army post in which one soldier and two guerrillas were killed.

The denial came ahead of Sunday's talks between Parbatya Chattagram Jana Sanghati Samity (PCJSS), the political wing of the rebel Shanti Bahini (peace force), and the Bangladesh government to end the decades old insurgency in the rugged hill region.
On May 3, tribal guerrillas fought a three-hour battle against the army after their bid to capture a marketplace and force the soldiers out of the post was foiled.
A statement released by the PCJSS said the Shanti Bahini was not involved in the shootout and was strictly observing a ceasefire agreed earlier with the government.

"The attack on the BDR (border guard) outpost does not arise as it (Shanti Bahini) has been strictly observing the ceasefire to maintain congenial atmosphere for restoration of permanent peace in Hill Tracts through dialogue," it said.
Government officials earlier expressed doubt that the guerrilla attack on the army post might torpedo the peace initiative between the government and the PCJSS.
Officials in the troubled Hill Tracts say a hardline group inside the Shanti Bahini is opposing any peace initiative with the government.

The Shanti Bahini, made up of mostly Chakma tribesmen, have been in a state of revolt since 1973, when Bangladesh rejected their demand for autonomy for the 5,500 sq mile (14,200 sq km) Hill Tracts bordering India and Burma.
Officials say more than 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency, which also forced some 55,000 tribespeople to flee into India.
Over 6,700 tribespeople returned home recently following an agreement between Bangladesh and India.
